Riemannian between- and within-group variances (VEG, VIG)

Source: R/validation.R
riemannian_variances.Rd

Estimates VEG = sum_i rho(mu_i, mu)^2 / (K-1) and VIG = sum_i sum_j rho(X_ij, mu_i)^2 / (n-K) using the Riemannian distance rho on Kendall's shape space.

Usage

riemannian_variances(X, cluster)

Arguments

X

Landmark array (k x 2 x n).

cluster

Vector of group labels, length n.

Value

A list with VEG, VIG, and the ratio VEG/VIG.

Details

The group and overall means are full Procrustes means: the dominant eigenvector of the complex sum of squares \(\sum_j z_j z_j^*\) of the pre-shapes (Kent, 1994). This is the Frechet mean under the full Procrustes distance.

References

Kent, J. T. (1994). The complex Bingham distribution and shape analysis. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 56(2), 285–299. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1994.tb01978.x

Examples

mu_list <- list(
  matrix(c(0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE),
  matrix(c(0,0, 20,0, 20,10, 0,10), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE)
)
out <- sim_landmark_gaussian(mu_list, c(15, 15), sigma = 1, seed = 1)
riemannian_variances(out$X, out$group)
#> $VEG
#> [1] 0.06036169
#> 
#> $VIG
#> [1] 0.01257175
#> 
#> $ratio
#> [1] 4.801375
#>
